metadata.title: Eli Raridon (thigh) downgraded to non-participant Thursday
metadata.description: Eli Raridon (thigh) was downgraded to a non-participant at practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The rookie suffered a thigh injury during last week's game. He was able to practice on Wednesday, but he was downgraded to a non-participant on Thursday and was unable to practice at all. It looks like he's trending the wrong way for Week 3, which could lead to more work for Hunter Henry against the Jaguars.

metadata.title: Eli Raridon - Limited to open week
metadata.description: Raridon (thigh) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Raridon was forced to leave Sunday's 20-3 win over the Steelers in the first half with a thigh injury, and he was unable to return to the game. The tight end's ability to practice in any capacity Wednesday is a positive sign, and he'll have two more chances to log a full practice before the team faces the Jaguars in Week 3.

metadata.title: Eli Raridon (thigh) limited at practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Eli Raridon (thigh) was limited at New England's practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: The rookie looked good in Week 2 before going down with a thigh injury. It doesn't seem to be a serious issue, however, as he was able to practice in a limited fashion on Wednesday. He looks like he could be a breakout candidate over the course of the season if he's able to stay healthy and on the field.

metadata.title: Eli Raridon limited in Week 2 due to a thigh injury
metadata.description: Patriots TE Eli Raridon caught his lone target for 30 yards in the Patriots' 20-3 win over the Steelers.
metadata.analysis: Rairdon exited the game after the reception and was originally listed as questionable to return. The rookie tight end remained out of the game and fantasy managers will want to monitor his status heading into a Week 3 matchup with Jacksonville.

metadata.title: Eli Raridon - Won't return Sunday
metadata.description: Raridon (thigh) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Steelers.
metadata.analysis: Raridon exited the game after hauling in a 30-yard pass from Drake Maye. The catch that caused the tight end to enter the medical tent was his only target in the contest.

metadata.title: Eli Raridon (thigh) questionable to return
metadata.description: Patriots TE Eli Raridon is questionable to return Sunday due to a thigh injury.
metadata.analysis: It is not immediately clear how Raridon suffered the injury. If the rookie is unable to return, Julian Hill will serve as the backup tight end to Hunter Henry.

metadata.title: Eli Raridon - Iffy to return vs. Pittsburgh
metadata.description: Raridon is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Steelers due to a thigh injury.
metadata.analysis: Raridon hauled in a 30-yard pass from Drake Maye before going to the blue medical tent to be evaluated for a thigh injury. Cameron Latu will serve as the backup tight end behind Hunter Henry for as long as Raridon is sidelined.

metadata.title: Eli Raridon Out for Remainder of Week 2 vs. Steelers
metadata.description: New England Patriots tight end Eli Raridon (thigh) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the visiting Pittsburgh Steelers, his team reported via the X platform. The rookie had one catch for 30 yards in Sunday's home game before sustaining the injury. Hunter Henry becomes New England's go-to tight end with Raridon out of the game.

metadata.title: Eli Raridon Questionable to Return With Thigh Injury
metadata.description: New England Patriots tight end Eli Raridon (thigh) is questionable to return against the Pittsburgh Steelers, according to Patriots Communications. The rookie had one catch for 30 yards before leaving the game. Hunter Henry remains New England's primary tight end and would take on an even larger share of the work if Raridon can't return. Cameron Latu is also available with Tanner Arkin inactive Sunday.

metadata.title: Eli Raridon Not Ready To Be Counted On in Week 2
metadata.description: New England Patriots backup tight end Eli Raridon caught his only target for two receiving yards in Week 1's loss to the Seattle Seahawks. The rookie out of Notre Dame is behind Hunter Henry on the depth chart but is on the field in two tight end sets. Nonetheless, it is hard to count upon Raridon at a loaded tight end position league-wide until he proves himself more. Henry eats up most of the tight end targets for the Patriots so Raridon will need to show more involvement in the passing game before he can be relied upon. The Patriots play the Steelers in Week 2 who have a good defense and limited Atlanta Falcons tight end Kyle Pitts to no catches in Week 1's win. This is not a good matchup for Raridon and it is really not wise to start him until he is coming off a big game.

metadata.title: Eli Raridon an Impact Player Around the Goal Line?
metadata.description: New England Patriots tight end Eli Raridon converted his lone target into a two-yard touchdown reception during his NFL debut in Week 1. The 22-year-old's low target total and 54% snap share indicate that he's not ready to pass Hunter Henry on the depth chart any time soon, but we have to wonder if he's still going to be a consistent threat to produce around the goal line. He was on the receiving end of the Patriots' only touchdown in the season opener, getting wide open as the defense paid attention to other offensive players. Managers should continue to monitor Raridon's usage and impact around the goal line, but in the meantime, he's not a bad player to speculatively add in deeper fantasy football leagues. He'll look to replicate his goal-line success while increasing his target share in Week 2 against Pittsburgh.
